newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Guatemala police probe brutal killings of four men.
newsitem.headline: Guatemala police probe brutal killings of four men.

text.p: A Guatemalan police investigating team is looking for the leaders of a mob that burned alive four men suspected of holding up a bus in a highland town, a police spokesman said on Thursday.
"An investigating team has gone up there to track down the instigators ... We are investigating who is responsible," National Police spokesman Luis Licks told Reuters.

An enraged mob broke into a police station where the suspects had been held, captured them, beat them and sprayed them with gasoline before setting them on fire, National Police director Angel Conte Cojulun told reporters.
The victims were identified as Oziel Calderon, 54, a painter; Pedro Calderon, 48, a dental assistant; Nery Calderon, 43, a painter; and Erwin de Leon, 34, an evangelical pastor.
Five police officers were injured in the melee, Conte said.

Police in Momostenango, about 330 miles (530 km) west of the capital, arrested the four men earlier on Wednesday on suspicion that they were members of a band of seven armed men that assaulted and robbed passengers on a bus earlier in the day.

According to local press reports, relatives of the four murdered men said they were not criminals, but four friends on a hunting trip. Other reports said witnesses from the bus holdup said they recognised the men.
Mob killings are common in Guatemala, where people are frustrated with an inept justice system and the legacy of impunity for criminals with money.
